made.name: Back bar
made.thesis:
My Bar stops being a wall of about 160 chips behind a Shelf/Drinks switch and becomes a bar you look at. Your bottles stand on lit shelves in the cabinet's wine lining, and under them is a paper counter showing what they pour. It's one screen and one scroll, so the payoff is always right under the bottle you just tapped.

Each object uses Cabinet's two materials:
- On the shelf: a lit, coloured bottle wearing a bone label clipped to the shelf edge.
- Not on the shelf: the same silhouette stamped into the lining, with no label.
- On the counter, drinks you can pour show their lit tungsten photo. Drinks one thing short show their unlit ghost photo (or the vector deboss face), grouped by the one thing you'd need to buy.

Adding a bottle swaps those ghost faces for lit ones. That swap is the "light up beneath" moment, and it's an image crossfade, not a layout animation.

All numbers in the mockup come from running lib/bar.ts's matching logic on the real barIndex.json and drinks.json:
- The 14 basics pour 47 drinks.
- The stocked 16-item shelf pours 52, with 214 drinks one thing short.
- Adding Campari lights 9: Agavoni, Americano, Boulevardier, Cardinale, Garibaldi, Jasmine, Lucien Gaudin, Negroni and Old Pal.
- Best next buys: Grenadine +9, Vodka +8, Grapefruit and Absinthe +7.
made.interaction:
FIRST OPEN (empty): the shelves are dark, with no backlight. The 14 basics stand stamped into the lining where they belong: spirits on the top shelf; vermouths, triple sec and syrup in the middle; bitters, soda, citrus and mint on the rail.
- One line says "Tap what you have. These 14 basics pour 47 drinks."
- Tap any ghost and it turns into a lit bottle with a label.
- "Add all 14 basics" (the bone primary button, since wine is 1.22:1 on lining) lights them all at once. "Search" opens the add sheet.
- The counter shows four unlit faces (Daiquiri, Martini, Old Fashioned, Mojito) with the line "Nothing yet. What you light comes up here, starting with these."

STOCKED:
- A shelf's backlight comes on once anything stands on it.
- Every owned bottle wears a mat label: "Gin", "Rye / whiskey" (two-word names past ten letters take two lines).
- The best next buy for each shelf stands unlit at the end of that shelf, with its payoff in words: "Vodka +8 drinks", "Grenadine +9 drinks", "Grapefruit +7 drinks".
- Tapping a lit bottle takes it off: it goes ghost in the same spot and nothing reflows, so tapping again undoes it. Tapping a ghost puts it on.
- Right under the shelves, "Pour tonight 52" updates and its subline names what changed: "Campari lit 9: Negroni, Boulevardier, Americano and 6 more." Those drinks lead the strip. VoiceOver hears "Campari on the shelf. 9 more drinks, 52 in all."

TONIGHT (the same screen scrolled to the counter):
- A strip of lit mounts (Margarita, Boulevardier, Tom Collins…), ordered: just lit, then "New" to your Dex, then A to Z. Each has its Dex status tag. Tapping one opens the drink page; "See all" opens the full list.
- "One thing short 214", grouped by the missing thing and ranked by how many drinks it pours. The top group is a card: an unlit grenadine bottle, "Pours 9 more drinks", an Add button, and the ghost faces of Tequila Sunrise, Ward 8 and Whiskey Daisy (vector, no photo), plus "6 more".
- The other groups are rows: "Vodka, Pours 8 more: Kamikaze, Lemon Drop, Screwdriver", each with Add. Add puts that bottle on its shelf, and its faces light and move up into Pour tonight.

ADD A BOTTLE (the search glyph's sheet, for the ingredients not on a shelf):
- The app's search field, then a row of shelf filter chips (Spirits, Liqueurs, Wine & beer, Bitters, Citrus, Syrups).
- "Worth adding" rows ranked by what each would pour with your current shelf, each with a small lining window holding its bottle: "Vodka, Pours 8 more · in 62 drinks". This replaces the wall of chips.
- "On your shelf" rows show a wine "On shelf" check toggle.
- Clear shelf moves here, behind the existing confirm.
made.how_to_build_in_rn:
STRUCTURE
- Same route, src/app/(tabs)/bar.tsx: one Animated.ScrollView, keeping useTabScroll('bar') for the tab-bar compaction and useScrollToTop.
- The SegmentedControl two-pane split goes away.
- The screen root is paper (colors.bg + Grain), so check-design rule 10 still holds.
- The back bar is the existing LiningBand with lip (in-flow 12pt shade onto paper), under ScreenTopBar size="lg" tone="lining". right = TopBarButton icon="search" label="Add a bottle". No second "+", since the tab bar already has one.

NEW FILES
- src/components/bar/BackBar.tsx:
  - Shelf: a row of bays, a plank View (6pt top face plus a 10pt front edge in the bar's espresso, with the 1pt counterLine highlight), and a 14pt VerticalFade shade under it. When the shelf holds at least one owned item, a VerticalFade backlight runs from colors.backlight to clear, ending at the plank. No text ever sits on it.
  - Bay: a memo'd Pressable keyed on (id, owned, pours), the same pattern as today's ShelfChip, so a tap re-renders one bay.
  - BottleArt: react-native-svg, already in the binary, so no new module.
  - ShelfTag: mat fill, 1pt matEdge, radius 3, textRole.statusWord 12/16 in ink, maxFontSizeMultiplier 1.3.
- src/lib/barArt.ts: a table mapping ingredient id to form, glass, liquid, label and cap. About 12 forms (square, slim, tall, whiskey, rye, wine, aperitif, squat, agave, dasher, small, siphon, plus fruit and sprig), with a fallback per category. Ghost is the same paths stroked in debossLight (upper) and debossShadow (lower), the tokens VectorFace's deboss already uses. Labels carry a rule and a small device, never words, so no brand is imitated.

SHELF LAYOUT
- Spirit goes on the top shelf; liqueur, wine and syrup in the middle; everything else on the rail.
- Bays are packed into planks in JS from worked-out widths: max(art width + 12, textWidth(label) + 12) via lib/textFit.ts, the same way dexStatusTagWidth sizes tags. Two-word labels split onto two lines.
- A full shelf starts another plank. No onLayout, so the first frame is final, and Dynamic Type adds planks instead of clipping.
- Order is a snapshot in a ref, re-sorted only on blur (useFocusEffect). Bottles never move while you're tapping.
- Each shelf gets at most one ghost suggestion: the top nextBest entry that belongs on it.

COUNTER
- Header: Inter shelfTitle "Pour tonight", a tabular count, and a wine "See all". It pushes a new route, src/app/bar/tonight.tsx, that hosts today's DrinkRow + ListGroup + ShowMore code moved over unchanged. It's a new route, so regenerate typed routes once with Metro on a unique port (v3.1 rule 6).
- Strip: a horizontal FlatList, at most 12 items, small initialNumToRender and windowSize. Each item is Mount size="shelf" + MountWindow + DrinkFace mode="lit" + DrinkName role=printName measure=100 + DexStatusTag.
- The "Campari lit 9" line: diff makeable ids in the toggle handler against a ref of the previous result, then call ui.tsx's announce() for VoiceOver.
- lib/bar.ts gains byMissing (nearly grouped by missing[0], largest first, top 6), computed in matchBar's existing pass and memoised by matchOwned.
- The first group is a Card with ghost thumbs (Mount size="thumb", DrinkFace mode="ghost": the 256px ghost photo, or VectorFace deboss). The rest are ListGroup/ListRow, with a lining window holding the ghost BottleArt. Add is Button variant="secondary" size="sm" with a plus.
- Add sheet: src/app/bar/add.tsx as a native formSheet route (UIKit presentation, not Reanimated). It reuses SearchField, searchIngredients, Chip filters (like the Dex's), ListGroup rows ranked by the full tally, and confirmDestructive for Clear shelf.

WHAT MOVES, AND WHY IT RESTS VISIBLE (three things, none on Reanimated or Animated.timing, no entering=)
1. Press lift: Bay uses Pressable's synchronous style callback, ({pressed}) => pressed && {transform:[{translateY:-2}]}. There's no animation driver at all, so a bottle is at rest the moment the finger leaves. I avoided PressableScale here because its withSpring is Reanimated.
2. Ghost to lit: when DrinkFace's source flips from the ghost photo to the lit one, expo-image's own transition={140} crossfades it natively (SDWebImage). If the transition never runs, the new image just appears. Set it to 0 under Reduce Motion. A vector-face drink flips instantly.
3. The existing native-driven tab-bar compaction.
- Every bottle, tag and drink is laid out at full opacity on the first frame, and nothing waits on a callback.

MEMORY AND THE TAB-SWITCH LAG
- Bottles are vectors: zero decoded bitmaps.
- The strip has at most 12 photo windows at 100×112, with enforceEarlyResizing and cachePolicy="disk". Groups use 256px ghosts.
- That's fewer image views than today's 40-row lists of DexThumbs, the 256 MB cap is untouched, and the tab mounts lighter than it does now.

NEW TOKENS (none carry text)
- colors.plankTop, colors.plankFace (= reelBar), colors.backlight.
- elevation.tag (the 1pt contact line), so rule 12 holds.

CHECK-CONTRAST ADDITIONS
- Tag ink on mat: about 14:1.
- Ghost names: onLiningMuted on lining is 6.79:1 (5.77 on the worst grain pixel). They sit in the plank's shade, which only darkens the ground.
- "+8 drinks" in onLining: 13.32:1.
- An assertion that backlight is never under text.

VOICEOVER
- Each bay is a button with a selected state: "Campari, on your shelf" / "Vodka, not on your shelf, pours 8 more drinks", hint "Double-tap to put it on (take it off)".
- Each shelf opens with a VoiceOver-only header: "Spirits, 5 bottles".

REUSED, UNCHANGED
LiningBand, VerticalFade, Grain, ScreenTopBar/TopBarButton, Mount, MountWindow, DrinkFace, VectorFace, DrinkName, DexStatusTag, Card, ListGroup, ListRow, Button, Chip, SearchField, announce, haptic.select, confirmDestructive, matchOwned/searchIngredients, useBar.
risks: Illustration is the real cost. About 160 common ingredients need convincing bottle art, and a weak set will read as clip art next to the tungsten photos. Mitigation: about 12 shared forms plus a per-id colour table with category fallbacks, reviewed as a headless-Chrome render sheet the way the glyphs are, then an eye pass from Jan.

The bar index has category bugs that would put things on the wrong shelf. ginger-ale, ginger-beer and ginger are filed as 'spirit' (ginger ale would stand among the spirits), and maraschino-cherry is filed as 'liqueur'. Fix this in scripts/build-bar-index.mjs and regenerate, never by hand. Also, dry-vermouth has uses = 0 (it only appears as a family expansion), so it's missing from COMMON_INGREDIENTS. The add sheet's browse must include family members or Dry vermouth vanishes from browsing.

The back bar grows with the shelf. A 30-bottle home bar is 5 or 6 planks, about 700pt, before the counter, and bar.tsx's own comment says returning users come back for the drinks. Past 3 planks the bar should fold behind 'Show all 31 bottles' (a plain conditional render, no animation), or the counter header should pin.

Taking a bottle off is a single tap, so mis-taps happen. It's softened because nothing reflows while the tab is focused (the same tap undoes it), and the counter line plus the VoiceOver announcement say what changed ('Gin off the shelf: 18 fewer'). Positions re-sort only on blur. If they re-sort on every change, bottles jump under the finger.

At accessibility text sizes, labels widen until there are only 1 or 2 bays per plank. Cap labels at 1.3 (VoiceOver still reads the full name) and check at the largest sizes in Jan's Release build. No agent can check this; there's no simulator.

Real bottle photos exist for only about 14 ingredients (both vermouths, the sherries, the ports), and dry-vermouth.webp shows a real brand label (Noilly Prat). Mixing photo bottles with vector ones on a shelf breaks the set, so shelves stay vector-only.

The 'light up' moment depends on expo-image's native transition when the source changes. A drink with no photo flips from deboss to lit with no crossfade. Accept that rather than faking it with Reanimated, which is the thing that stalled build 15.

SVG mount cost: about 30 bottles at about 14 nodes each is around 420 react-native-svg nodes the first time the tab opens. Memoise each bay and measure tab-switch time on Jan's phone in a Release build, since that lag is the bug Jan reported.
Dropping the Shelf/Drinks segmented control changes a habit. The full drinks list moves to a pushed 'See all' route, which needs a typed-routes regeneration.
Count semantics: 'in 62 drinks' and 'pours 8 more' count the 899 recipes in barIndex, not the 2,089-drink Dex. Wording like 'named in 62 recipes' may avoid a mismatch with Dex totals.

made.name: Tonight
made.thesis:
Today My Bar opens on the work and hides what you get for it. The Shelf pane is the default: a wall of about 160 chips in 13 category sections. What you can make sits behind a segmented control, as text rows with 44pt thumbnails. "Worth buying next" is a row of chips with bare numbers. Tonight turns that around, and the screen becomes one place with no segments.

It opens in the cabinet's lining with the question "What can I make tonight?" and its answer: "72 drinks", followed by the drinks themselves as big tungsten-lit cards. Each card is a 280pt photo on the cellar ground, named in Playfair. It lists the bottles from your own shelf that the drink uses, and carries the Dex plates ("#0127", "+ New to your Dex").

Below the cards, on paper, comes "One thing away". Each row is one ingredient, with its count and its best-known drink ("Grenadine: 10 more drinks, like Tequila Sunrise"), and a one-tap Add. After the tap, the row shows the drinks it just added, right where you tapped.

Stocking the bar becomes a guided photo picker. Bottles are photo tiles, most-used first, and every tile you have not ticked says what it would add to your shelf right now ("+6 drinks"). A live footer counts as you tap ("36 drinks tonight. Rye whiskey added 5"). The first open puts the payoff first: "The basics alone make 47, like these", three real cards and one Add the basics button.

The copy says "One thing away", not "one bottle away", on purpose. The existing code notes that the missing thing is as often lime, mint or egg white as a bottle.

Every number in the mockup comes from src/data/barIndex.json, run through matchBar's own logic (counts.cjs): 14 basics give 47; a 20-item shelf gives 72; Grenadine adds 10, Absinthe 8, Grapefruit 8; adding grapefruit takes it to 80. Every tile photo is a drink whose recipe really uses that bottle.
made.interaction:
First open (empty shelf):
- The lining band asks "What can I make tonight?" and shows three lit cards the basics would make (Daiquiri, Old Fashioned, Martini, then "44 more").
- One tap on Add the basics puts the 14 starter items on the shelf. The screen redraws in the same commit as Tonight with 47 drinks.
- Or you tap bottle tiles inline: Gin, Sweet vermouth, White rum, Vodka, Rye whiskey, Brandy, most-used first. Each tile shows a + badge, and once ticked a wine check, a 2pt wine ring and the words "On your shelf". The state never rests on colour alone.

Picker ("Your shelf" sheet), opened from "Your shelf 20" or Edit:
- At the top: a search field over all 493 ingredients, then jump chips with how many you own in each group (Bottles 5, Fresh 4, Syrups and bitters 2, Mixers 1).
- Bottles are a 3-column photo grid. Fresh things, syrups and mixers stay the existing ShelfChips.
- Every unticked tile shows what it adds to your shelf right now (Triple sec "+6 drinks"). When it adds nothing, it shows its overall use ("in 28 drinks").
- Each tap answers instantly: a haptic select, and the footer's count rewrites itself ("36 drinks tonight", "Rye whiskey added 5"). VoiceOver announces the same sentence.
- Show me closes the sheet and returns Tonight to All, at the top. Clear asks first, as today.

Tonight (stocked shelf):
- Swipe the cards sideways. They snap one at a time, and the next card peeks 132pt.
- Tap a card to open the drink page. Tap its "+ New to your Dex" plaque to open it in the Dex.
- Style chips on the lining filter the cards in place (All 72, Sours 25, Spirit-forward 16, Highballs 16, Fizzes 3).
- The search glyph and the last "All 72" card open the alphabetical list. That list is today's DrinkRow list, unchanged.

One thing away:
- Tapping Add puts the ingredient on your shelf. The button becomes a selected "Added" toggle (tap again to take it off).
- The row grows a strip of the drinks it just added (Greyhound, Salty Dog, Siesta, +5 "See all 8"). The figure updates, and VoiceOver hears "Grapefruit is on your shelf. 80 drinks tonight, 8 new."
- The list keeps its order until you leave the tab, so nothing jumps under your finger. It re-ranks on the next focus.

Your shelf (at the foot):
- Your bottles appear as small photo tiles and the rest as chips. Tapping a bottle filters the cards to what that bottle makes.
- Scrolling down compacts the tab bar exactly as today (frame 4).
made.how_to_build_in_rn:
Files: rewrite src/app/(tabs)/bar.tsx; extend src/lib/bar.ts; add src/components/bar/{TonightCard,BottleTile,AwayRow}.tsx, src/app/shelf.tsx (the picker, presentation 'modal' like log.tsx) and src/data/bottleFaces.ts. No native module, no install, no Supabase change.

Engineering rule held throughout: nothing animates content in, and nothing waits on motion to appear.

Screen skeleton
- The fixed bar is ScreenTopBar size="lg" tone="lining" title="My Bar", with a TopBarButton icon="search". It shows its liningLip rule from useScrolledPast and keeps FocusedStatusBar light. This is the Home pattern.
- Under the bar sits one Animated.ScrollView. It keeps today's wiring: useTabScroll('bar', onScrolledPast), useScrollToTop and the TAB_BAR_CLEARANCE padding, so the tab-bar compaction is still the existing native-driven Animated.event (identity at offset 0, off while VoiceOver runs).
- The first child is a LiningBand with lip and shade="inFlow" (cabinet.tsx), holding:
  - the question, in textRole.prose onLiningMuted;
  - the figure, in textRole.heroFigure via HeroFigure, beside a Button variant="onLiningOutline" size="sm" with the bottle icon;
  - the style chips;
  - the card carousel.
- After the band come the paper sections. The root keeps <Grain />.
- The SegmentedControl, the Shelf pane and the Drinks pane leave bar.tsx. The alphabetical list (DrinkRow plus ShowMore, as today) moves to a pushed route opened by search and by the "All 72" card. A new route means regenerating the typed routes on a unique Metro port, per spec rule 6.

Cards
- A horizontal FlatList, not a ScrollView: initialNumToRender 3, windowSize 3, snapToInterval 292, decelerationRate 'fast', scrollsToTop false. No removeClippedSubviews (specs/06 cause 4).
- TonightCard is a liningDeep View: radius 12, a 1pt liningLine edge, elevation.seat.
- The photo is DrinkFace mode="lit" at 278x278, which already uses expo-image with cachePolicy 'disk', enforceEarlyResizing and a liningDeep window. A 1024px photo decodes at 834px on a 3x phone, so it stays sharp, and it falls back to VectorFace for the 1,927 unphotographed drinks.
- Over the photo's top edge: MediaNumberPlate and DexStatusPlaque, with onPress opening the Dex.
- The name is DrinkName with textRole.nameLg, measure 248 and cap 1.3. Below it, an Inter onLiningMuted line of the shelf ingredients the drink uses.
- The whole card is wrapped in PressableScale, the house rule for media tiles, and opens /drink/[id].
- The cards sit on the cellar, never over a scrim, so no text depends on photo pixels.

Style chips
- Chip in ui.tsx gains tone?: 'paper' | 'lining'. On lining it has a liningControl edge with onLining ink; selected, an onLining fill, lining ink and the check (13.32:1).
- Labels come from styleLabel(subcategory) plus a small plural map, which satisfies check-design rule 8.
- Filtering happens in memory, over the memoised result.

lib/bar.ts
matchOwned keeps its identity memo. matchBar gains four things:
- `used` for each makeable drink: the owned id that met each slot, which feeds the ingredient line.
- `gains`: for the single missing slot, credit EVERY id in it, not just slot[0]. This feeds the picker's "+N". The current canonical tally says Rye +0 when Rye actually adds 5. Full-slot credit matched a brute-force recount for 9 bottles.
- `rankTonight`: drinks not in your Dex first, then photographed (drinkPhoto(id) != null), then lowest dexNumber. Stable, never rarity.
- A headline drink for each nextBest ingredient, chosen by the same rule.

nextBest stays canonical, so the One thing away list never shows bourbon and rye as two rows for the same drinks.

One thing away
- A ListGroup of AwayRow. Leading is DexThumb (photo or vector face). The title is the ingredient label in Inter SemiBold. The subtitle is Inter with only the drink name in textRole.nameInline.
- Trailing is the existing Chip as a toggle: label "Add" with icon 'plus', and selected "Added" with the check, wine on wineWash. Chip already ticks haptic.select.
- The tap calls useBar.toggle(id) and announce().
- The expanded strip renders in the same commit: up to three 68pt mounted thumbs with DrinkName tileName, measure 68, plus a "+N" tile that pushes the filtered list. No LayoutAnimation, no `entering`.
- Row order is a snapshot held in a ref and re-ranked on focus (useIsFocused), so counts update in place without a reorder.
- At the foot sits "Show 4 more", the same stepping as today's ShowMore.

Your shelf
- A 4-column grid of BottleTile size="sm" for owned bottles, then the existing ShelfChips for everything else.

Picker (src/app/shelf.tsx)
- Root Grain, a header with "Clear" (Button dangerText, which asks via confirmDestructive) and a close TopBarButton, then SearchField (searchIngredients, unchanged).
- Jump chips use Chip and call scrollToLocation.
- The body is a virtualized SectionList. The Bottles section is chunked into rows of 3 BottleTiles; the other sections are ShelfChip wraps.
- BottleTile is a PressableScale holding:
  - a square expo-image window, enforceEarlyResizing, radius 8;
  - a 24pt badge, + on onMedia.markerFill or a wine check;
  - an outer 2pt wine ring drawn on paper, 12.33:1;
  - the label, and its "+N", "in N drinks" or "On your shelf" line.
  - Its spoken label: "Gin, on your shelf, pictured Martini".
- The faces come from bottleFaces.ts: about 40 hand-curated ingredient-to-drink ids (the vermouths map to their own catalogue photos). A small check script fails any entry whose recipe does not use that ingredient or that has no photo.
- The sticky footer is a plain View outside the list. It shows the matchOwned count and the last toggle's diff, which bar.ts already has to compute, and a primary Button "Show me" that calls router.back() and resets the filter.

Empty state
- Same LiningBand. The preview cards are matchBar(new Set(STARTER)) memoised once at module level, giving "47".
- Add the basics is a Button variant="onLining" that calls add(STARTER).
- The first 6 BottleTiles appear inline, with "See every ingredient" opening the sheet.

What moves, and why it rests visible
1. The carousel and the strips move only under the finger (native scroll with snapping). Every card is laid out and opaque from its first frame.
2. Tab-bar compaction is today's scroll-linked native transform. It is identity at the top.
3. The picker is a native react-native-screens modal: UIKit animates the container and the content is never hidden.
4. Press feedback is PressableScale, which respects Reduce Motion and rests at 1. Even a stalled spring leaves a fully visible 0.97 tile; it never gates content.
5. Selections, counts and the expanded strip swap in a single render. There is no count-up and no fade.
6. The only fade is expo-image's existing 140ms decode transition over the liningDeep window. Text and controls never wait for it.

Tab-switch cost
The first focus mounts fewer views than today's 160 chips: 3 cards, about 4 rows and about 10 tiles. matchBar stays a single memoised walk of the 899 recipes, and the 3 hero decodes are each about 2.8 MB, well inside the 256 MB expo-image cap.

check-contrast.mjs gains these pairs: lining chip 13.32 and 3.27 for its edge; card text on liningDeep 14.47 and 7.38; wine on paper 12.33.
risks: There is no bottle photography in the catalogue: only the two vermouths are bottles. The other tiles show each bottle's signature drink, and someone could read that photo as 'you can make this'. Mitigations: the label, a spoken 'pictured: Martini', and a checked bottleFaces map. The real fix is about 40 bottle photos baked through the existing tungsten pipeline.

The current nextBest tally undercounts family members because it credits only slot[0]. Rye shows +0 when it actually adds 5. The picker's +N must use full-slot credit (verified against a brute-force recount). The One thing away list stays canonical, otherwise bourbon and rye would appear as duplicate rows for the same drinks.

Generated data quirks would show up on screen. In barIndex.json, ginger beer and ginger ale are categorised as 'spirit', so they would become photo tiles in Bottles. Dry vermouth has uses=0, so it would read 'in 0 drinks'. The fix belongs in scripts/build-bar-index.mjs: drinks data is never hand-edited.

Rows stay in place after an Add and re-rank only on the next focus. Counts can therefore sit out of order for a while: after adding grapefruit, Maraschino liqueur jumps to 13 but stays below rows of 7. That trade is deliberate, chosen over rows jumping under the finger.

The hero ranks 'New to your Dex' first, and that reads the collection store. If the ranking runs before the store hydrates, the cards reshuffle at launch. Rank only once the store is hydrated, or rank by dex number alone and leave the Dex state to the plaque.

The carousel is virtualized, so with Dynamic Type a card mounted later can be taller than the ones already shown (a two-line name at a large size) and the row height changes mid-swipe. Reserve name lines from the current fontScale, and limit the ingredient line (not a drink name) to 2 lines.

Putting the lining band and its top bar on My Bar extends v3 section 9.1.2, which reserves tone="lining" for Home. It is a spec change Jan has to approve. It also needs the light status bar while the tab is focused, and its overscroll should show lining, not paper.

Dropping the Shelf and Drinks segments changes the IA. Clear shelf moves into the sheet, and the alphabetical list moves to a pushed route. New routes mean regenerating the typed routes on a unique Metro port, and no agent can run the app, so the swipe, the snapping, the sheet and VoiceOver order all wait for Jan's Release-build pass.

PressableScale runs on Reanimated, which is the stack that stalled in Release. A stall here can only leave a tile at 0.97, never hidden. If Jan wants zero Reanimated on this tab, use the pressed-opacity fill instead.
The copy 'One thing away' departs from the brief's 'one bottle away'. It is more honest, because the missing item is often lime, mint or egg white, but Jan should choose the wording.

made.name: Cards: swipe to stock, then a back bar that pours
made.thesis: Today, filling My Bar means working through a wall of about 160 chips sorted by type, and that is the job that keeps people from using it. Cards changes the job. On first open the tab is a deck of 24 common bottles and fresh things, and you answer each one with a flick: Have it or Skip. The deck lives in the wine lining as bone card stock, so it looks like the rest of the Cabinet. Each card shows a real catalogue photo (the ingredient's own bottle if the catalogue has one, otherwise a famous drink that uses it). It also shows a true count ("In 168 drinks") and what saying yes gets you right now ("Adds 6 you can make now, like the Gin and It"). The payoff ticks up in the progress row as you go, and the shelf is built in about a minute. After the deck, the tab is one page. At the top is a compact visual back bar: two ledges of drawn bottles and fresh items, each labelled. Under it is the number of drinks you can make tonight, then galleries by style (Sour 17, Spirit-forward 12). Last is "Worth buying next", grouped by the one missing ingredient, so the shopping question gets its answer straight away: vodka gives you 10 more drinks, and here they are. The Shelf/Drinks segmented control, the two long lists and the separate chip section are gone. Search over all 493 ingredients stays one tap away for people who know their bar.
made.interaction: First open (shelf empty): the My Bar tab shows the deck, card 1 of 24 (Gin). Swipe right or tap Have it to put it on the shelf. Swipe left or tap Skip to pass. The card follows your finger and tilts slightly, and a "Have it" stamp fades in as you drag right. Let go past about 96pt (or flick) and the card is gone; the next card is already sitting fully drawn behind it. Let go short of that and the card snaps back upright. Each answer updates the progress row ("7 of 24 · 5 on your shelf · 4 drinks") and VoiceOver announces the new count. "Undo White rum" puts the last answer back. "Done" ends the deck early. "Search 493 ingredients instead" opens the old searchable chip picker as its own screen. Stocked shelf: two ledges (Bottles; Fresh and mixers) that scroll sideways. Tap a bottle for a native action sheet: "Remove Campari from your shelf" or "Show drinks with Campari". "Deal more cards" opens the next deck (liqueurs, wine, the fridge). Below the shelf: "53 drinks you can make tonight" with See all (a pushed grid), then one sideways rail per style in Dex order. Each card is a mount with its photo or lit vector face, the name in Playfair, and a New or In your Dex tag. Tapping one opens the drink page. scores.verdict: Winner. It's the only direction where My Bar turns into a place rather than a feed. In the stocked frame, lit bottles with bone mat labels stand on backlit shelves in the wine lining, and each shelf ends with an unlit next buy ('Vodka +8 drinks', 'Grenadine +9 drinks'). The tungsten Pour tonight strip sits right under the bottle you tapped. It reads as Cabinet itself (lining, mat, deboss ghosts), not as a borrowed pattern, and it's the most premium and least AI-looking of the three. Interaction is one tap: ghost to lit, nothing reflows, and tapping again undoes it. It also follows the engineering rules best. Press lift uses Pressable's synchronous style with no Reanimated, the only fade is expo-image's native crossfade, and the bottles are vectors with zero decoded bitmaps, so the tab mounts lighter than today. That directly addresses the tab-switch lag Jan reported. made.thesis:
The first thing a new person sees is a question, not a form. "What do you drink?" sits above big re-lit catalogue photos lying loose in the wine lining. Each tap moves a drink from one material to the other, which is the Cabinet's own idea: the loose print (LoosePrint) becomes a bone mount (Mount, mounted, onLining) with its number plate and "In your Dex". At the same moment a mini mount drops into one of three recessed slots in a tray pinned above the tab bar. The person spends about ten seconds building something before being asked who they are, and the provider sheet then puts their own three drinks above it ("Your Dex has begun · 3 of 2,089") where the generic Negroni, Zombie and Last Word sit today. So the account step reads as "keep going", not "fill in a form". Returning people are never forced through it: "Sign in" sits top right from the first frame.

One honest correction to the brief: the account cannot "save" the Dex. The Dex lives on the phone. It is AsyncStorage "drinkdex-collection", there is no collection table in supabase/schema.sql, and Settings' reset copy already says the Dex and the account are separate. So the picks go into the Dex on this phone as they are tapped, and every line of copy says "start" or "has begun", never "save" or "back up". If Jan wants an account to carry the Dex to a new phone, that is a migration plus sync, a separate project.

Why these five sign-in options and no more. Sipply is iPhone-only, so everyone holding it has an Apple ID: Sign in with Apple covers the whole install base, adds Hide My Email for the private ones, and goes first, as guideline 4.8 and the HIG require when Google and Facebook are offered. Google covers the most common personal email account and anyone who came from Android. Facebook is the network the app already uses for Find friends (FacebookFriends.tsx), so signing in with it also brings in friends. Phone number covers people with no social account, or who won't link one. Email is the fallback that always works, and its password and reset steps already exist. All five are already built in store/auth.ts: Apple through signInWithIdToken, Google and Facebook through openOAuth, phone through OTP, email through password. So this direction adds zero providers, zero native modules and zero Supabase changes.

Not added, and why:
- Instagram no longer offers a consumer login.
- X, TikTok, Snapchat, Microsoft, LinkedIn and Discord each need an SDK or a new Supabase provider, and they reach people already covered by Apple, Google or phone.
- Every extra 48pt row pushes email and the consent text under the tab bar on a 6.1-inch phone.
- Passkeys would be good later, but they need a native module this build cannot add.

made.how_to_build_in_rn:

- The only moving thing is native scrolling. The picker list must NOT register with ScrollChrome's useTabBarCollapse: the bar stays full, and the tray, which is placed for the full bar, never floats over a compacted one.
- The scrolled-bar hairline is a boolean flipped in onScroll past 1pt, not a fade.

made.name: The door
made.thesis:
Today's screen is a form with a wine band above it. The door makes the first screen the catalogue itself, so a new person sees what they're joining before they're asked anything. The whole screen is a back bar: three columns of the tungsten re-lit catalogue photos, each print a 148x185 rounded rectangle with a 1pt printEdge and its real name in Playfair on a foot scrim (Aperol Spritz, Negroni, Clover Club, Zombie, Paloma, Old Fashioned...). The columns drift slowly, the outer two up and the middle one down. The wall fades into the cellar ground, and the one bold Playfair line, the "Sipply" wordmark at 88pt, sits over that fade. Under it is one Inter line: "2,089 drinks on the wall. Start your Dex with the next one." A bone (mat) card holds the ways in, and the terms are pinned under it.

Playfair stays for the wordmark and drink names only, so the hero line is the wordmark and not a sentence. There are no pills: the grabber is a 1pt-radius rectangle. No glows: every gradient is a photo scrim or the photo-to-ground dissolve.

Nothing waits on motion. On the first frame Apple, Google and Facebook are already tappable and the terms are visible. Phone and email are one tap or one swipe away, behind an explicit text row, not a hidden gesture.

The door also hides the floating tab bar. A tab bar says you're already inside, and its 94pt would come out of the wall. "Look around first" (an outlined rectangle top right) replaces the close X and goes to the Dex, which works signed out, or back on pushed routes, as onClose does today.

Why these five ways in and no more:
- Sign in with Apple reaches every person who can install the app, because it's iPhone-only. It's one Face ID tap, it can hide the email, and it's the privacy-preserving login that App Review 4.8 requires beside any third-party sign-in. It goes first, in Apple's black style, at the same size as the others, as Apple's HIG asks.
- Google is the most widely held account after Apple's.
- Facebook is the one Meta login that still exists (the old Instagram login API was retired in 2024), and it's the app's existing route to friends (lib/facebook.ts).
- Phone needs no third-party account and feeds Find friends with the verified number.
- Email is the universal fallback.

Each further provider would reach nobody new. Anyone with an X, Microsoft, Discord, TikTok or Snapchat account also has an Apple ID, a phone and an email. TikTok and Snapchat aren't even built-in Supabase providers. Each one costs another console, another branding rulebook, another review and another support path, and another button that dilutes the choice. Five is the most that fit on one card without a scroll.

made.how_to_build_in_rn:
No new native modules and nothing installed. Everything below is RN core Animated with the native driver, react-native-svg gradients, expo-image, and expo-apple-authentication's own button (already in the binary).

New file: src/components/auth/Door.tsx. SignInScreen renders it for step 'entry' in place of CabinetSheet backdrop='full'. Every other step keeps CabinetSheet compact, unchanged.

Tree:
- Ground: a View on colors.liningDeep with FocusedStatusBar light.
- DoorWall, absolute and full screen, pointerEvents none, accessibilityElementsHidden.
- The dissolve: a react-native-svg LinearGradient from cellar 0 to 1, FIXED at the rest position (restTop-330 to restTop). It sits outside the ScrollView so the scroll clip never seams it.
- The dim: an Animated.View on liningDeep, opacity = scrollY.interpolate([0, open/2], [0, .62], clamp).
- The top scrim, 172pt and fixed.
- An Animated.ScrollView, framed from insets.top + 44 to the bottom, with snapToOffsets [0, open], decelerationRate 'fast', automaticallyAdjustKeyboardInsets, and onScroll = Animated.event(contentOffset.y -> scrollY, {useNativeDriver:true}). Its content is:
  - a spacer holding the wordmark (a new textRole wordmarkHero, Playfair Bold 88/92, maxFontSizeMultiplier 1) and the lede (prose 17/24 in onMedia.ink);
  - the card: mat, 12pt top radius, 1pt matEdge, the upward elevation.sheet;
  - in the card: the grabber, the Apple button, ProviderButton google, ProviderButton facebook, the disclosure row, the existing PhoneEntry unchanged, and ProviderButton email.
- A pinned footer with the existing <Consent lead="By continuing">, inside a KeyboardAvoidingView so it rides above the keyboard.
- The top row with "Look around first": a liningControl 1pt edge on an 80% cellar fill.

restTop is computed from the fixed button heights (50pt each) plus the disclosure row's measured height. open is the content end. When they collide (SE-class windows or accessibility text sizes), the spacer collapses and the door simply starts open.

What moves:
1. The scroll itself. It's UIKit, so it can't stall.
2. Scroll-linked, native-driven interpolations, all of them identity at offset 0: the column parallax (translateY = -k*offset, clamped at open), the dim, the print-name opacity (one interpolation shared by every name's Animated.View), and the chevron rotation.
3. The drift: one Animated.loop(Animated.timing(drift, {toValue:1, duration:96000 / 120000, easing: Easing.linear, useNativeDriver:true})) per direction. Each column's translateY = Animated.add(drift.interpolate([0,1],[0,-SET]), parallax).

Why it rests visible: each column holds its six prints twice, so every frame of the loop is a complete wall. The wall is drawn in place at its start offset on the first frame. Nothing awaits a completion callback, and no button, text or touch depends on the loop. A stall, a missed start, Reduce Motion or VoiceOver all leave a still, complete wall, which is the rest state.

The loop starts only while the scene is focused (useIsFocused from expo-router, as saved.tsx does) and AppState is active. It is stopped with stopAnimation on blur or background, and never started with Reduce Motion on or VoiceOver running. It needs a one-file allowlist entry in check-design rule 15, with that argument as the reason.

The disclosure row calls scrollTo({y: atOpen ? 0 : open, animated:true}). JS state (atOpen, from onMomentumScrollEnd) drives only accessibilityState.expanded and haptic.select(), never visibility. The phone Field's onFocus scrolls so that Continue's bottom clears the footer.

Providers:
- Apple: AppleAuthentication.AppleAuthenticationButton (buttonType CONTINUE, buttonStyle BLACK, cornerRadius radius.control, height 50). iOS draws the logo, font and title, so Apple's rules hold by construction. While pending, a same-size black overlay with an ActivityIndicator covers it.

- Email: the existing secondary skin with the mail glyph.

There is one print size, so a repeated photo shares one decode.

This loop gates nothing, but if Jan wants zero timers anywhere, ship the wall still: the scroll-linked parallax alone still makes the swipe feel alive.

made.name: First pour
made.thesis:
Before Sipply asks for an account, it should hand the person a drink. The welcome is one big empty coupe on a cellar counter. It is the Dex tab's own coupe icon, enlarged and drawn from SHAPES.coupe. Hold it and it fills. At the brim the line drawing cuts to a real tungsten-lit photograph of one of the 24 photographed coupes, shown with its Dex number and name. That is the Cabinet's own metaphor (an empty recess becomes a lit drink) played once before sign-up, so the first thing someone does in the app is the thing the app is about. The pour gates nothing. From the first frame, every way in already sits in one stacked bone card under the stage. After a pour, the card's top line ties the two together: "Join, and we'll start you on a Last Word" (once onboarding finishes, that drink's page opens). People coming back on the same phone get a compact Welcome back: their last pour as the stage, their five latest catches, and one button for the method they used last time.

Why these five ways in and no more:
- Sign in with Apple goes first. Guideline 4.8 requires it whenever Google or Facebook is offered, and every person on this iOS-only app already has an Apple ID.
- Google is the largest account base outside Apple.
- Facebook brings the social graph that FacebookFriends already uses to find friends.
- Phone number is for people who want no third party at all.
- Email is the universal fallback, and it is the reset path.

Between them, everyone with an iPhone has at least two. X, TikTok and Microsoft would add buttons, SDKs and review surfaces but almost no people who lack all five (Microsoft is mostly work accounts). Instagram no longer offers a consumer login. Each extra row would push the card below the tab bar on 6.1-inch phones.

Note for Jan: v3-cabinet.md §1.1 lists "Sign-in sheet keeps its layout" as a standing rule. His new request replaces it for the first step, so that line in the spec needs updating to match. The later steps (code, email, password, reset) keep the sheet unchanged.

Phone moves from an inline form to its own step. That is one extra tap for phone sign-ups, the trade for showing all five ways in above the tab bar.
There is no real tilt. expo-sensors is not in the binary, and adding it is a native module. 'Tilt/tap' becomes hold to pour and tap to splash. If Jan wants physical tilt, it waits for a native build.

The pour is JS-timer driven. During cold start (intro film, auth refresh) it can step rather than glide. It never hides anything, but it is the one place the interaction could feel less polished than intended. The fully native fallback is a pull-down on the stage (Animated.event + interpolate, native driver).

The cut from drawing to photograph only lines up if the photos frame their coupes alike. They roughly do (rim about 34%, foot about 85%), but not exactly. Either measure the rim and foot per photo in build-drink-photos.mjs, or accept a small jump at a deliberate cut.
liquidColor() is wrong for these drinks (Last Word comes out pink, Paper Plane green). The pour colour has to come from the photo pipeline, or the reveal contradicts the pour.

App Review 1.4.3: a pouring toy in an alcohol app could read as gamified drinking. Keep it to a single reveal: no counts, streaks, scores or 'pour more' copy. The 18+ consent line stays on the card from the first frame, and the drinks shown are already public in the signed-out Dex.

Google's branding guidelines name Roboto Medium for the button label. The app ships only Inter and Playfair. Either add Roboto Medium as a font asset (expo-font, not a native module) for that one label, or accept Inter (common practice, low risk).

Welcome back keeps a name, handle, avatar and drink ids on the phone after sign-out. That matters on shared phones and reveals that an account exists. It needs 'Forget this account', clearing on deletion, a mention in the privacy policy, and possibly a 'Sign out and forget' choice at sign-out (Jan's call).

'Join, and we'll start you on a Last Word' is a promise. If firstPourId is lost between sign-in, the username step and Welcome, the copy lies. It needs a test path through all three gates (Home, Profile, pushed profile).

Height budget: at 6.1-inch heights the stage must drop to 168pt to keep Apple, Google and Facebook above the floating tab bar at rest (Apple asks that its button never need a scroll). This has to be verified on Jan's phone in a Release build, since agents cannot run the app.

scores.verdict: The only direction where the sign-up is made of the Cabinet itself. A tap turns a loose print into a bone mount with its number plate, and the tray fills. The person builds something before the form appears, and the sheet then shows their own three drinks. It looks expensive and specific to Sipply, not like a template. Nothing animates. It uses real Cabinet parts (LoosePrint, Mount, NumberPlate, DexStatusTag), keeps the tab bar, and has no pills or uppercase. The cards are about 198pt, so the 1024px photos stay sharp at 3x, which matters given the HD complaint. Ease of use is the weak spot: a new person needs three picks, Continue, then a provider. A person who wants to join without picking can only use 'Sign in', a label meant for returning users. The same picker also gates the Profile tab. The five full-width rows push email and the consent text under the tab bar on 6.1-inch phones. Buildable with no new modules, but it touches collection.ts (seed and unseed must skip the celebrations and need a unit test), signInFlow, ProviderButton and CabinetBackdrop. Its honesty about 'start' versus 'save' is correct.

The easiest of the three. All five ways in are on the first frame in one compact bone card: Apple, Google and Facebook full width, then phone and email side by side, with the consent text above the tab bar. Hold-to-pour is a good tactile toy, and it gates nothing because the level rests wherever the finger lets go. The welcome-back screen (last pour, latest catches, one tap with the last method, 'Use another way', 'Forget this account') is the best idea in the round. Its weaknesses are looks and house rules. The first frame is a flat line-art coupe with a flat liquid fill, which reads more like a generic illustration than the re-lit tungsten photography, and the cut from vector to photo puts a drawing beside photos, which the v3 rules avoid. The hero photo runs about 440pt wide, so a 1024px source is upscaled. Last Word and Paper Plane already look soft, which is the exact complaint Jan made about Profile. The drink you are 'started on' is chosen by the pour, not by you, so the play means less. Hold-to-fill needs a per-frame level driver (Reanimated shared value or a JS frame loop) driving an SVG path, plus a VoiceOver alternative to the hold gesture.

The most cinematic first frame: a full-bleed wall of real prints with Playfair names, an 88pt wordmark over the dissolve, and Apple, Google and Facebook tappable at once. The swipe that parts the columns at different rates is a nice depth effect, and it rests at identity. But the interaction is mostly watching, and 'logo over a blurred photo wall with a social-login sheet' is a common login pattern, so it is the least Sipply-specific of the three. It breaks the most rules. It needs an Animated.loop drift exemption, and build 15's native timing already stalled on Jan's phone. It hides the floating tab bar by editing FloatingTabBar, the file behind the tab-switch lag Jan is reporting. It decodes about 14MB of prints, against the budget rule that no screen mounts more than it does today. Home and Profile each mount a wall. The solid #0866FF Facebook button is the loudest thing on the bone card. Measured snap detents, keyboard plus pinned terms on SE heights, and the native Apple button not scaling with Dynamic Type add risk.

scores.verdict: WINNER. This is the only direction where nothing animates. Every pick is a same-frame state swap from LoosePrint to Mount, and the empty slot fills in place inside a fixed-height row. Rule 15 passes untouched, and a stall in a Release build has nothing to stall. It builds from Cabinet parts that already exist (LoosePrint, Mount, NumberPlate, DexStatusTag, CabinetSheet, signInFlow's instant cut), keeps the tab bar, and adds no providers, native modules or Supabase changes. Apple is listed first, then Google, Facebook, phone and email, and all of them already exist in store/auth.ts. The rendered frames show the most interactive idea of the three: the person builds a Dex before any form appears, and the sheet reflects their three drinks back to them. The copy is honest that the Dex is device-local. Costs I checked in the repo: (1) seed() must skip collection.unlock()'s celebrate() and set bestRung silently (collection.ts lines 155-180), so it needs a unit test. (2) About 20 MB of decoded prints is under the Home tab's 58 MB budget in v3-cabinet section 11, but AuthGate also renders in Profile and about 8 pushed routes, so the picker must be limited to Home or unmounted on blur. Otherwise Jan's tab-switch lag comes back. (3) Phone gains a tap. (4) On a 6.1-inch phone, email and the consent text sit under the tab bar. (5) Photo-less seeded entries water down "in your Dex". Jan should decide that one.

Runner-up. It is the easiest to use: every way in sits on the first frame inside one bone card, the tab bar is kept, phone and email share one row, and only one photo is decoded at a time. The weak part is the feature that was meant to make it immersive. Hold-to-pour is a novelty with a random payoff. The level rises with time while the finger is down, which is a timed animation: RN Animated.timing breaks check-design rule 15, and Reanimated withTiming is the engine that stalled. It does rest visible and gates nothing, so a stall only leaves a half-full glass. A line-drawn coupe beside the re-lit photographs is off-material for Cabinet. Every drink is poured into a coupe but then cuts to its real photo, so a Negroni would pour into a coupe and land in a rocks glass, unless the random drink is limited to coupe glassware (drinks.json has glassware but no liquid colour, so colours would be hand-authored). VoiceOver needs an accessibilityAction in place of the hold. The welcome-back card keeps @handle, avatar and Dex count on the phone after sign-out, and auth.ts already worries about shared phones (line 596). The full written spec was truncated in the brief, so I judged this from the four rendered frames and index.html.

The most cinematic of the three: an 88pt wordmark over a parallax wall of real prints. It also has the best provider compliance. The Apple row is the native AppleAuthenticationButton, so Apple's rules hold by construction, and Google's light-theme tokens are exact. Apple, Google and Facebook are all tappable on the first frame. But it breaks the engineering rules that build 15 earned. The drift is Animated.loop(Animated.timing), which check-design rule 15 forbids by name, so it needs an exemption to the rule written after the tab-slide stall. It hides the floating tab bar by editing FloatingTabBar, so signed-out people lose the bar. It decodes about 14 MB of prints in every AuthGate scene: Home, Profile and every gated pushed route. Jan's complaint is lag when switching tabs, and this puts a moving photo wall in two tabs. It also brings snapToOffsets with a measured detent, a pinned footer inside a KeyboardAvoidingView, snapping turned off for VoiceOver, a loop gated on focus and AppState, and native-driven interpolations that can lag a frame. None of that can be tuned without a device, and no agent can run the app. The only interaction is a swipe that reveals phone and email; the wall itself is decoration.

grafts: From the door: unmount the picker grid when its scene loses focus (useIsFocused, as saved.tsx does), and render the taste picker only in the Home tab. Profile and the gated pushed routes (record, saved, stats, activity, post, user, reel) get the plain provider sheet. That way two tabs never hold a mounted photo grid at once, which is the lag Jan just reported.

From the door: work out the tray height and list paddingBottom from fixed sizes plus fontScale, not from the first onLayout, so the grid's bottom padding never jumps once on mount (the door's restTop rule).

From the door: use its exact Google light-theme tokens (googleEdge #747775, googleInk #1F1F1F) and its contrast pairs (white on #0866FF 4.82, #747775 on mat 4.27) in the ProviderButton skins and check-contrast. Keep the native AppleAuthenticationButton (BLACK, CONTINUE, cornerRadius radius.control) as a ready drop-in if App Review questions the custom left-aligned Apple row.
From the door: take the phone country default from the device region (Puerto Rico +1 here), so the extra tap to reach phone costs as little as possible.

From the pour: put 'Phone number' and 'Email' side by side as one half-width pair, falling back to one column when fontScale > 1.3. That saves about 58pt so the consent text clears the floating tab bar on 6.1-inch phones, fixing the tastes direction's own risk.

From the pour: when someone signed out on this phone, put the method they used last first on the 'Welcome back' sheet, with 'Use another way' under it. Store only the method name, never the @handle, avatar or Dex count, because shared phones are a known concern in auth.ts.

From the pour: give the sheet a title that names the person's own drink in Playfair (nameInline), e.g. 'Your Dex has begun with a Piña Colada'. It shows people that a real catalogue drink started their Dex, at no cost.
